top_choice_rationale: P001 meets the test I apply: an original idea (the magic-wavelength lattice), a realized instrument, independent replication across laboratories, and concrete new measurements (geodesy-scale redshift, constants tests, many-body clock physics). The credit can be stated in two names, Katori and Ye, provided the citation is anchored to the lattice clock and its demonstrated control of light shifts and collisions, not to precision spectroscopy in general. P003 follows because the HgTe quantum-well experiment is a convincing original experiment, though the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang leaves a credit problem. P002 is a real and mature discovery, but I cannot confirm which individuals did the original work among large collaborations, with Double Chooz left out. Any award is preferable to no award.
